newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada auto union choses GM as second target.
newsitem.headline: Canada auto union choses GM as second target.

text.p: The Canadian Auto Workers union said on Monday it chose General Motors Corp.'s Canadian unit as the union's next bargaining target, with a strike deadline of midnight Oct. 2.
On Sunday the CAW's Chrysler members overwhelmingly ratified the tentative agreement reached last week with Chrysler Corp.'s Canadian unit.

The Chrysler deal gave the union unprecendented protection against the shifting of work to outside suppliers, or outsourcing, and set the stage for a battle between the CAW and GM, which has plans to farm out more than 5,500 jobs.
CAW President Buzz Hargrove said the union will not compromise on the strong deal reached with Chrysler and is determined to reverse GM's decisions to shift work to outside suppliers.
"We're determined to reverse these decisions as we head to the bargaining table with GM," said Hargrove. "GM will accept the pattern. The only question is when."
Talks between the two sides were set to begin Monday in Toronto. GM officials were not immediately available for comment.

Hargrove told reporters the union will work hard to reach a settlement with GM in the nine days before the strike deadline, but he acknowledged it would be "very, very difficult to get a settlement without a strike."

He said the union was considering an "escalated" strike plan if an agreement was not reached by Oct. 2, rather than striking all plants at once. Under the graduated strike plan, work would be halted at some plants, while others initially remained open.
Hargrove said the graduated plan would best protect the 28,510 GM Canada members from the personal financial impact of a strike.
"We'd like to limit the exposure on our members, their families and the community, while at the same time putting maximum pressure on GM," said Hargrove.

He said the union will hold a convention on Oct. 18 to approve a special dues assessment on the total union membership to provide GM workers with strike pay in case of a protracted strike at the Oshawa, Ontario-based automaker.

Hargrove said his choice of GM as the second target in Canada will not interfere with the bargaining schedule of the United Auto Workers in the United States. The UAW membership is expected to complete its ratification voting on Sept. 29 of the tentative agreement reached last week with Ford Motor Co.
